column3: summary
column4: help

column3: the compiler could not prove a complete access set
column4: The runtime must serialize conservatively; remove dynamic or opaque access if parallel execution is required.

column3: multiple modules define the same declared package export
column4: Keep exactly one module definition for each exported function.

column3: an asset display name literal is not a valid asset name
column4: Use a non-blank name of at most 128 characters without `#`, `@`, or control characters.

column3: authorization was written as an arbitrary string
column4: Declare `permission Admin;` and use `authorize(Admin)`, or explicitly choose `authorize(anyone)`.

column3: an authorization clause follows the return type
column4: Write authorization before the return type: `kotoage fn name(params) authorize(Admin) -> Type { ... }`.
column5: kotoage fn bump(int delta) -> int authorize(anyone) {\n    return delta;\n}
column6: kotoage fn bump(int delta) authorize(anyone) -> int {\n    return delta;\n}

column3: the source contains an invisible bidirectional control character
column4: Delete the character; inside a string literal that genuinely needs it, write it as a `\\u{...}` escape. Bidirectional controls make reviewed text read differently from what compiles.

column3: expression branches have different types
column4: Make every if or match branch tail produce exactly the same type.

column3: break appeared outside an accepted bounded loop
column4: Move break into the body of a compiler-proven bounded for loop.

column3: linked modules disagree on one ordinary enum identity
column4: Use one exact declaration schema for each locked package, source unit and enum name.

column3: one nominal error identity has conflicting variant schemas
column4: Use the same exact error descriptor for a locked package identity; different schemas require distinct declared identities.

column3: a Japanese word resembles a branded keyword but is not one
column4: Write the keyword exactly: 誓約/seiyaku, 言挙げ/kotoage, 始まり/hajimari or 改善/kaizen. Both spellings of each keyword are the same token and may be mixed freely.

column3: a compile-time integer appeared outside a bounded List capacity
column4: Use the compile-time integer only as the second argument of List<T, N>.

column3: a const initializer depended on runtime evaluation
column4: Initialize the const from literals and previously declared constants only.

column3: continue appeared outside an accepted bounded loop
column4: Move continue into the body of a compiler-proven bounded for loop.

column3: The imported compiled contract failed canonical artifact admission.
column4: Build the contract with the current compiler and supply its complete authenticated .to artifact in the owning source inventory.

column3: The declared compiled contract is absent from its source owner inventory.
column4: Supply the referenced .to artifact through the owning project inventory and use its exact relative path in import seiyaku.

column3: the imported contract reference has no callable public method with this signature
column4: Use the admitted interface method with its declared parameter labels. Lifecycle hooks are unavailable through imported references.

column3: an exact decimal exponent has invalid spelling
column4: Write at least one base-10 digit after `e` or `E`; a leading exponent sign is allowed.

column3: an exact decimal literal has invalid spelling
column4: Use base-10 digits, at most one decimal point, an optional decimal exponent, and underscores only between digits.

column3: an exact decimal value exceeds the signed 512-bit mantissa limit
column4: Reduce the magnitude so the unscaled canonical mantissa fits the signed 512-bit domain.

column3: an exact decimal value exceeds the 28-digit canonical scale limit
column4: Reduce the significant fractional precision to at most 28 digits. Trailing fractional zeros are canonicalized away before this limit is checked.

column3: a function, kotoage, view or lifecycle hook declaration has the wrong shape
column4: Public functions are `kotoage fn name(...)` (also `言挙げ fn`) or `view fn name(...)`; the lifecycle hooks are written `hajimari() { ... }` and `kaizen() { ... }` with no `fn` and no name.

column3: a reusable dependency is not a module source unit
column4: Change the dependency to exactly one module declaration; only the package root may be deployable.

column3: an expression whose branches all diverge lacks an exact result type
column4: Provide an exact contextual type, or use the construct as a statement when every branch returns from the enclosing function.

column3: a numeric divisor is zero
column4: Use a nonzero divisor or validate it before the operation.

column3: a source-unit declaration name was repeated
column4: Rename or remove the repeated declaration; V1 has one unambiguous namespace per source unit.

column3: linked typed modules reused a compiler-owned HIR identity
column4: Report this compiler defect with the complete source graph; source cannot assign HIR identities.

column3: an import alias is repeated in one scope
column4: Keep one explicit package binding for each import alias.

column3: linked modules define the same localization message key more than once
column4: Keep one canonical message for each localization key in the linked graph.

column3: one package declares the same module name more than once
column4: Give every module in the package a unique canonical name.

column3: a named call argument is repeated
column4: Supply each declared parameter exactly once.

column3: the locked graph contains the same package identity more than once
column4: Keep one canonical record for each package identity in the locked dependency graph.

column3: a package graph contains duplicate normalized logical source paths
column4: Remove the duplicate or give each source a unique normalized logical path.

column3: different logical sources received the same compiler-owned source identity
column4: Report this compiler defect with the complete normalized source graph.

column3: a struct literal field is repeated
column4: Supply each declared struct field exactly once.

column3: a struct pattern names the same field more than once
column4: Bind each struct field once; aliases must also use distinct local names.

column3: a locked package contains no Kotodama modules
column4: Add at least one module source or remove the empty package from the locked graph.

column3: typed linking produced no root or reusable module program
column4: Provide one seiyaku root and every explicitly imported non-empty module package.

column3: an English concept word is written where a branded keyword declares the concept
column4: Use the branded keyword in either spelling: a deployable unit is `seiyaku`/`誓約`, an authorized state-changing function `kotoage fn`/`言挙げ fn`, the activation hook `hajimari`/`始まり` and the in-place replacement hook `kaizen`/`改善`.

column3: ordinary enum variants cannot declare rejection messages
column4: Use explicit named codes in an ordinary enum; use error enum only for raisable failures.

column3: the ordinary enum descriptor is not canonical
column4: Declare between 1 and 256 uniquely named variants with distinct nonzero u32 codes.

column3: an error message violates the static message contract
column4: Use one nonblank static UTF-8 message between 1 and 4096 bytes on each annotated error variant.

column3: an error type has an invalid nominal schema
column4: Declare one error enum identity with unique names and nonzero u32 variant codes.

column3: native events belong to their declaring seiyaku
column4: Declare the event and emitting helpers in the seiyaku; modules export reusable value types and pure or explicit ledger helpers.

column3: emit requires a declared native event record
column4: Write `emit Event { field: value };` with every declared field exactly once.

column3: the native event payload or declaration inventory is invalid
column4: Use canonical public value fields, excluding Json, StateCursor and private values recursively; declare at most 256 events within 65536 encoded bytes.

column3: an event declaration is not an ordinary value type
column4: Use `emit Event { field: value };`; declare a struct for reusable values and use it as an event field.

column3: an exact terminating quotient needs more than 28 fractional digits
column4: Use `div_round` with an explicit representable scale, or change the operands.

column3: source uses an identifier spelling forbidden in every Kotodama V1 context
column4: Choose a domain-specific identifier; lowercase `amount` remains an ordinary business identifier.

column3: a bounded for-loop initializer lowered to more than one operation
column4: Use one simple let binding or expression as the for-loop initializer.

column3: a bounded for-loop step lowered to more than one operation
column4: Use one simple let binding or expression as the for-loop step.

column3: a full-width form of an ASCII character appears outside a string or comment
column4: Replace it with the ASCII character; switch the input method to half-width (direct input) for code. The ideographic space U+3000 is accepted between tokens.

column3: an expression-valued if omits its else branch
column4: Add an else block whose tail has exactly the same type as the then block tail.

column3: an expression-valued if let omits its else branch
column4: Add an else block, or use if let as a statement when no value is needed.

column3: an immutable binding was assigned after declaration
column4: Declare a mutable local with `var`, or compute the final immutable value before binding it.

column3: runtime int and decimal values were mixed without a named conversion
column4: Convert the int with decimal::from_int(value) before decimal arithmetic or comparison. Exact numeric literals may still infer their type contextually at compile time.

column3: source includes form a cycle
column4: Remove an include edge so every fragment expands through an acyclic include graph.

column3: an exact numeric conversion would discard a fractional part
column4: Use an explicitly truncating or rounded conversion when loss of precision is intentional.

column3: source attempted to call a compiler-internal raw capability
column4: Use the typed namespaced source API; allocation, pointers, raw syscalls, and opaque instructions are unavailable.

column3: typed numeric operands violated the compiler's canonical operator matrix
column4: Report this compiler defect with a minimal source reproducer; no artifact is emitted from inconsistent typed HIR.

column3: typed analysis received inconsistent or incomplete resolved-HIR metadata
column4: Report this compiler defect with the source; resolution must assign stable identities and targets before typed analysis.

column3: a compiler intrinsic was used outside its declared operation context
column4: Use the public namespaced operation that owns the intrinsic instead of referring to the compiler-owned value.

column3: an integer literal is outside the signed 512-bit domain
column4: Use a value from -2^511 through 2^511 - 1.

column3: checked integer arithmetic overflowed
column4: Change the inputs or use an explicit wrapping operation when modular arithmetic is intentional.

column3: an assignment targeted a non-assignable expression
column4: Assign only to a `var` binding, a field of one, or `map[key] = value`. To change a StateMap entry, copy it with `var entry = Map.get(key).expect(Error::Missing);`, change `entry`, and store it back with `Map[key] = entry;`.

column3: a package, module, alias, or symbol name is not a strict V1 identifier
column4: Use a valid unambiguous Kotodama V1 identifier in the reported graph location.

column3: a typed identifier literal is malformed or encoded for another network
column4: Copy the identifier exactly as printed, or re-encode an account for this network with `iroha tools address convert`. Canonical account literals write katakana half-width, except ヰ and ヱ.

column3: a reusable module contains a deployable-only declaration
column4: Move state, triggers, `kotoage`/`言挙げ`, `view fn`, `hajimari`/`始まり`, or `kaizen`/`改善` declarations into the seiyaku root.

column3: an exact numeric operation received a scale outside zero through 28
column4: Choose an int scale from 0 through 28.

column3: a logical module source path is non-canonical or escapes its package
column4: Use a normalized relative logical path contained by the package source root.

column3: a bounded collection operation exceeded the 64-item V1 limit
column4: Reduce the collection or split the operation into deterministic calls of at most 64 items.

column3: a native JSON object or array exceeds the per-node V1 bound
column4: Use at most 64 object entries or array elements at each JSON node; split larger data into bounded nested nodes.

column3: a native JSON object repeats a decoded key
column4: Keep each decoded key exactly once; identifier and quoted spellings of the same key still collide.

column3: a Json::parse string literal is not valid JSON
column4: Provide one valid JSON value and keep every decoded object key unique.

column3: Json::parse requires a direct string literal
column4: Use a direct JSON string literal so it is validated at compile time, or construct dynamic typed values with native `json { ... }` and `json [ ... ]` syntax.

column3: a native JSON construction exceeds a recursive V1 ABI bound
column4: Reduce recursive object, array, Option, or List structure so the canonical construction schema fits its node, word, depth, and encoded-byte limits.

column3: a value cannot be converted by native JSON construction
column4: Handle Result and arbitrary structs explicitly, and keep StateMap, Secret, and other resource handles outside JSON.

column3: a kanji keyword is joined to the following word without a space
column4: Insert a space after the keyword, for example `言挙げ fn`.

column3: an identifier is a near-miss spelling of a keyword
column4: Correct the spelling; the suggestion is the closest keyword, and branded keywords are offered in both spellings.

column3: a kotoage function does not name the permission its caller needs
column4: Choose a declared permission with `authorize(Admin)` or explicitly allow every caller with `authorize(anyone)` before the return type.

column3: source uses a retired name for the quantity JSON getter
column4: Use value.get_quantity(key); typed JSON getters are receiver methods that return Option<T>.

column3: an Option or Result constructor or pattern is not spelled canonically
column4: Use Option::some(value), contextual Option::none, Result::ok(value), or Result::err(value) in expressions and match patterns.

column3: a mutable local is written `let mut`
column4: Declare mutable locals with `var`; `let` bindings are immutable.

column3: a hajimari or kaizen declaration declares caller authorization
column4: Remove `authorize(...)`; activation and in-place replacement are authorized by the runtime, not by the hook.

column3: a List capacity is outside 1 through 64
column4: Choose a compile-time capacity from 1 through 64.

column3: a List capacity is not a compile-time integer
column4: Use an integer capacity constant from 1 through 64.

column3: a list comprehension may exceed its contextual or V1 capacity
column4: Reduce the source capacity or use a context large enough for the full proven maximum, up to 64.

column3: a list comprehension filter is not boolean
column4: Use a bool expression after if; filters do not reduce the proven capacity.

column3: a list comprehension source is not a bounded List
column4: Iterate a List<T, N> so the compiler can prove the maximum result size.

column3: List.contains requires canonically comparable elements
column4: Use an element type with deterministic structural equality; resource handles and other non-comparable values cannot be searched with contains.

column3: a list expression conflicts with its contextual type
column4: Use a matching List<T, N> context and exactly assignable element values.

column3: an empty list literal has no element or capacity context
column4: Add a List<T, N> annotation to the binding, argument, or return position.

column3: a List index has the wrong type
column4: Use an int index with get or try_set.

column3: a list literal exceeds its contextual capacity
column4: Increase the declared capacity up to 64 or reduce the literal element count.

column3: a bounded List method has the wrong argument count
column4: Use the declared method signature and account for the implicit receiver.

column3: a mutating List method was called on a non-mutable receiver
column4: Bind the List with var before calling try_set, try_push, or pop.

column3: push follows initialization of a provably full List
column4: Declare an explicit larger capacity at initialization, remove an element first, or handle the Result from try_push. Unknown lengths and escaped aliases retain their runtime bounds checks.

column3: a List element contains a resource handle
column4: Keep StateMap, Secret, and other resource handles outside List elements.

column3: List.take received a dynamic limit
column4: Pass a compile-time integer limit so the result capacity remains proven.

column3: List.take received a limit outside its source capacity
column4: Use a constant limit from 0 through the source List capacity.

column3: List has an invalid number of type arguments
column4: Declare List<T, N> with one element type and one capacity constant.

column3: source attempted an unchecked List index operation
column4: Use get(index) for reads and try_set(index, value) for writes.

column3: local module imports form a cycle
column4: Remove an import edge so local modules have an acyclic dependency graph.

column3: a local binding duplicates or shadows another visible symbol
column4: Rename the binding so every local and source-unit declaration remains unambiguous.

column3: resolved call metadata was internally inconsistent
column4: Report this compiler defect with a minimal source reproducer; malformed resolved calls never produce artifacts.

column3: a match expression repeats a variant pattern
column4: Keep exactly one arm for each variant in the matched sum family.

column3: a match expression has no arms
column4: Add the complete namespaced pattern set for the matched Option or Result.

column3: a sum match omits an active or inactive variant
column4: Cover both Option variants or both Result variants explicitly.

column3: a match arm uses a `_` wildcard pattern
column4: Name every variant: `Option::some(value)` and `Option::none`, or `Result::ok(value)` and `Result::err(error)`; bind an unused payload as `_`.

column3: a parameter, state, constant or field declaration names no type
column4: Write the type before the name, for example `fn run(int value)` or `state int count;`.

column3: a package export names no module function
column4: Define the exported function in exactly one module or remove the stale export.

column3: a named call omits a required parameter
column4: Supply every required argument, positionally where the call accepts it or as `label: value`.

column3: a value-returning function does not return on every path
column4: Return the declared type on every reachable path or use one final block-tail expression.

column3: a struct literal omits a declared field
column4: Supply every declared field; field order in source is unrestricted.

column3: a struct pattern does not account for every field
column4: Bind or explicitly discard each field, or add a final `..` marker.

column3: one diagnostics request contains more than one deployable seiyaku root
column4: Keep one project root; check unrelated seiyaku roots in separate requests.

column3: a named parameter was supplied positionally
column4: This builtin takes labelled arguments: write each one as `label: value`, or pass a variable spelled exactly like the label. Single-argument calls, receiver methods, and pure helpers accept positional arguments.

column3: a named call supplies a later optional parameter after omitting an earlier optional ABI slot
column4: Supply the earlier optional parameter too, or omit the complete trailing optional suffix.

column3: a value converted to quantity is negative
column4: Use decimal when the value may be negative, or prove the value non-negative before an explicit quantity conversion.

column3: integer square root requires a nonnegative operand
column4: Pass a nonnegative int to math::isqrt; negative inputs fault instead of narrowing or changing sign.

column3: a NumericSpec, Mintable, or SignatureScheme argument is not a compile-time value
column4: Write the value directly as the argument: `NumericSpec::unconstrained()`, `NumericSpec::integer()`, or `NumericSpec::fractional(scale)`; `Mintable::Infinitely`, `Mintable::Once`, `Mintable::Not`, or `Mintable::Limited(tokens)`; `SignatureScheme::Ed25519`, `SignatureScheme::Secp256k1`, or `SignatureScheme::MlDsa`.

column3: a Unicode space other than U+3000 separates tokens
column4: Replace it with an ASCII space; tokens are separated by ASCII whitespace or the ideographic space U+3000.

column3: source used a retired, flat, or compiler-internal builtin spelling
column4: Use the canonical V1 namespaced builtin shown by the diagnostic.

column3: a numeric value was not in canonical int, decimal, or quantity form
column4: Construct the value with the exact canonical numeric type and representation.

column3: an explicitly rounded numeric operation received an unknown rounding mode
column4: Use one of the seven V1 modes: toward_zero, away_from_zero, floor, ceil, nearest_even, nearest_away, or nearest_toward_zero.

column3: an explicitly rounded numeric operation has the wrong number of arguments
column4: Pass every declared argument, positionally or by its declared label; rounded division requires divisor, scale, and mode.

column3: an explicitly rounded numeric method was called on an unsupported receiver
column4: Use decimal.div_round, quantity.div_round, or quantity.ratio_round with the operand types declared by the V1 numeric matrix.

column3: a typed-module package graph exceeds a fixed V1 frontend budget
column4: Reduce the package source count or aggregate source bytes before linking.

column3: locked package imports form a dependency cycle
column4: Break the cycle and keep the typed-module package graph acyclic.

column3: a namespaced pattern belongs to the wrong sum family
column4: Match Option values with Option::some/none and Result values with Result::ok/err.

column3: a sum pattern binds a payload on an inactive variant or omits an active payload binding
column4: Bind or explicitly ignore active payloads; write Option::none without a payload.

column3: a sum pattern was applied to a non-Option/non-Result value
column4: Use namespaced sum patterns only with Option<T> or Result<T, E>.

column3: the pattern variant does not belong to the expected type
column4: Match a variant from the exact nominal enum or sum type of the scrutinee.

column3: a grant or revocation did not name an instance permission declaration
column4: Pass a declared instance permission identifier as `permission:`. Chain imports, strings and dynamic Name values cannot be used for scoped grants.

column3: a permission declaration is invalid or outside a seiyaku
column4: Declare an instance permission with `permission Admin;` or import a chain token explicitly; modules cannot declare permissions and `anyone` cannot be a permission name.

column3: a positional argument follows a named argument
column4: Supply the positional prefix first, then named arguments in any order.

column3: a positional-only parameter was supplied by name
column4: Omit the label for parameters declared as `Type _ name`.

column3: a positional parameter follows a named parameter
column4: Place every `Type _ name` parameter before the named `Type name` parameters.

column3: a struct uses retired positional construction
column4: Use `Type { field: value, shorthand_field }`; apply the diagnostic fix when one is available.

column3: a struct is destructured by position
column4: Use `let Type { field, other: alias, .. } = value;`; positional patterns are for tuples.

column3: a Musubi project manifest is malformed or unsafe
column4: Use Musubi.toml with relative in-project source paths and a matching Musubi.lock.

column3: positional source paths cannot grant module linking authority
column4: Use musubi check --manifest-path Musubi.toml with declared imports, modules, exports, and packages locked by Musubi.lock.

column3: the Musubi project or locked dependency graph could not be reloaded
column4: Fix and save Musubi.toml, then resolve dependency changes with musubi check before continuing project analysis.

column3: a source module belongs to more than one contract target
column4: Select the intended target with musubi lsp --manifest-path Musubi.toml --contract <target>.

column3: postfix propagation is used outside a matching sum-returning function
column4: Return the same Option or Result family from the enclosing function, or handle the value explicitly.

column3: Result propagation would require implicit error conversion
column4: Use the exact enclosing Result error type or convert the error explicitly before propagation.

column3: postfix propagation was applied to a non-sum value
column4: Apply ? only to Option<T> or Result<T, E>.

column3: a public parameter name cannot be represented in the canonical call schema
column4: Use an ordinary canonical identifier such as permission_token; keyword spellings are not valid ABI field names.

column3: the nominal `quantity` type cannot be negated
column4: Use `int` or `decimal` for signed values.

column3: quantity does not define a remainder operation
column4: Use exact division, quantity.div_round, or quantity.ratio_round with an explicit scale and rounding mode.

column3: quantity subtraction would produce a negative result
column4: Change the operands, or convert to decimal explicitly when a negative result is part of the domain.

column3: a typed core query received bytes or the wrong identifier type
column4: Pass the exact AccountId, AssetId, AssetDefinitionId, DomainId, or NftId required by the query.

column3: a typed query page limit is outside 1 through 64
column4: Choose a page limit from 1 through 64.

column3: a typed query page window is outside the non-negative signed 64-bit range
column4: Use an offset in 0..=i64::MAX and ensure offset plus limit fits i64.

column3: a typed query page has invalid offset or limit arguments
column4: Pass named offset: int and limit: int arguments.

column3: QueryPage was instantiated with a view outside the declared core query set
column4: Use QueryPage only with a canonical core query view supported by ABI V1.

column3: a typed core-query projection was assigned to an incompatible result type
column4: Receive singular queries as Option<View> and plural queries as QueryPage<View>; raw byte compatibility is not part of the five V1 core-query families.

column3: an account quorum is outside the protocol's nonzero 16-bit domain
column4: Use an int from 1 through 65535. This is a protocol-field bound, not the range of Kotodama int.

column3: a loop uses an `a..b` range operator
column4: Count with `range(N)`, which iterates 0 up to N - 1 with a compile-time bound; offset the index for other starting points.

column3: exact decimal division has a nonterminating result
column4: Choose decimal.div_round, quantity.div_round or ratio_round, or mul_div_round for a fused product, with an explicit scale and rounding mode.

column3: a declaration collided with a reserved language or builtin name
column4: Choose an ASCII identifier that is not a V1 keyword, type, namespace, or builtin.

column3: an import alias collides with a compiler-owned capability namespace
column4: Choose a non-reserved explicit alias for the imported package.

column3: a fallible Result value was left unhandled
column4: Handle the Result with match, return, or propagation using ?, or explicitly discard it with let _ = expression;.

column3: a typed declaration is written `name: Type` instead of the type-first `Type name`
column4: Place the type before the name, for example `fn add(int lhs)`, `state int value;`, `const int limit = 1;` or `let int count = 0;`.

column3: source calls a retired width-specific or generic numeric helper
column4: Use exact operators, named int/decimal/quantity conversions, or native `json { ... }` construction.

column3: a numeric literal uses a retired suffix
column4: Use an unsuffixed literal in an explicit int, decimal, or quantity context; Kotodama V1 has no numeric literal suffixes.

column3: a declaration uses a retired numeric type name
column4: Use `int`, `decimal`, or the nominal non-negative `quantity` type.

column3: source calls a non-canonical trigger lifecycle operation
column4: Use ledger::trigger::register or ledger::trigger::unregister; the diagnostic provides an exact replacement.

column3: source used the retired multi-argument VRF verification form
column4: Encode one VrfVerifyRequest as bytes and pass it through the named request argument.

column3: a returned value does not exactly match the declared return type
column4: Return the exact declared type; use an explicit conversion where the V1 API provides one.

column3: the deployable package root is not a seiyaku/誓約 source unit
column4: Declare exactly one seiyaku/誓約 in the root and keep reusable dependencies as modules.

column3: secret data was used by an ordinary arithmetic operation
column4: Use only an approved proof or commitment operation whose secret-flow contract is explicit.

column3: a secret value influenced public control flow
column4: Remove the secret-dependent branch or loop.

column3: a scalar-register crypto operation attempted to consume Secret<T>
column4: Use crypto::valcom or another approved full-width proof operation that declares a Secret<T> flow.

column3: secret data reached a public host operation
column4: Pass only approved public proof or commitment outputs to ledger, context, state, and debug APIs.

column3: a secret value flowed into a log
column4: Remove the log or log only a public value independent of the secret.

column3: a commitment mixed secret data with an unapproved public value
column4: Use the exact approved commitment signature and explicitly public domain-separation inputs.

column3: a private input used a type outside the approved Secret<T> payload set
column4: Choose a supported fixed-layout secret payload type accepted by the ZK proof interface.

column3: a private input had no inferable Secret<T> payload type
column4: Use a type-first binding such as `let Secret<int> value = crypto::private_input(0);`.

column3: a private-input operation did not initialize an approved Secret<T> binding
column4: Initialize an explicit Secret<int>, Secret<decimal>, or Secret<quantity> binding.

column3: a private-input index depended on secret or unbounded data
column4: Use a public compile-time-bounded private-input index.

column3: a kotoage/view/hajimari/kaizen parameter was declared as Secret<T>
column4: Read private inputs through the ZK-only private-input API; public ABI records cannot contain secrets.

column3: a secret value flowed into a public return
column4: Return only an approved proof, commitment, or public value independent of the secret.

column3: Secret<T> was used outside a ZK seiyaku build
column4: Compile through a ZK-enabled project policy and keep the value inside approved proof or commitment operations.

column3: a secret value flowed into a durable-state key
column4: Use a public canonical key independent of all private inputs.

column3: secret-tainted data reached durable state
column4: Persist only an approved public commitment or proof result independent of raw secret material.

column3: durable state was declared with a secret-bearing type
column4: Keep Secret<T> ephemeral and store only approved public commitments or proof outputs.

column3: a secret value flowed directly into durable state
column4: Persist only an approved commitment or proof output.

column3: secret data reached an operation without an approved flow specification
column4: Use an operation explicitly listed by the V1 secret-flow policy.

column3: secret data was passed through a call whose flow behavior is unknown
column4: Pass secrets only to compiler-known proof and commitment functions with declared flow behavior.

column3: a declared source dependency is absent
column4: Supply the referenced file inside the explicit source bundle and use its canonical relative path.

column3: one fragment is assigned to multiple source units
column4: Give each fragment a single owning contract or module; use exported module declarations for shared dependencies.

column3: a source dependency has the wrong unit kind
column4: Use a bare declaration fragment for include, a module for import, and a seiyaku as the contract entry file.

column3: scalar durable state is not initialized on every normal `hajimari`/`始まり` path
column4: Assign every reported scalar state on all branches and before every early return; loop-only and short-circuited writes are not definite.

column3: scalar durable state was declared without a hajimari/始まり hook
column4: Declare hajimari/始まり and initialize every scalar state value before any normal return or fallthrough.

column3: a StateMap was treated as an in-memory first-class value
column4: Access the declared StateMap directly through get, set, remove, or bounded iteration.

column3: a StateMap key lacks a canonical deterministic Norito representation
column4: Choose a supported scalar canonical-Norito key type.

column3: a StateMap read discarded the possibility that its key is absent
column4: Use map.get(key), handle the returned Option<V>, and use map[key] = value only for writes.

column3: a local declaration shadowed durable state
column4: Rename the local declaration; V1 rejects all shadowing.

column3: a struct pattern places its rest marker before another field
column4: Place one `..` marker at the end to explicitly discard unspecified fields.

column3: a named struct pattern has a different nominal type from its initializer
column4: Use the initializer's declared struct type and bind its fields by name.

column3: an active-only sum constructor has the wrong payload count
column4: Supply exactly one active payload to Option::some, Result::ok, or Result::err.

column3: an active-only sum constructor has invalid source form
column4: Write Option::none without parentheses and give active constructors exactly one positional payload.

column3: a sum constructor conflicts with its contextual type
column4: Use the matching Option or Result constructor and an exactly assignable active payload.

column3: an inactive or partially inferred sum value lacks an exact type context
column4: Add an Option<T> or Result<T, E> annotation so every generic payload type is known.

column3: a block-tail expression does not exactly match its required type
column4: Make the final expression the exact required type or terminate it with a semicolon when the block returns unit.

column3: a Kotodama test actor was not a static literal alias
column4: Pass a string literal or Name::parse literal actor alias to the test helper.

column3: test invocation arguments do not match the target parameters
column4: Pass a closed typed record, for example `arguments: { count: 7 }`, with exactly the target parameter names and types. Use `{}` for a target with no parameters. JSON values are not accepted.

column3: a `test::` builtin was called outside a test function or a test-module helper
column4: Call `test::` builtins from a `#[test] fn` or from a private helper of a `*.test.ko` module that declares `koto_test { target: "..." }`; seiyaku code, including its private helpers, cannot call them.

column3: a runtime test helper targeted a private function
column4: Target a kotoage, view, hajimari, or kaizen declaration.

column3: a runtime test helper target was not a static literal
column4: Pass the kotoage, view, hajimari, or kaizen name as a string or Name::parse literal.

column3: a #[test] function has a public, parameterized, or value-returning signature
column4: Declare each test as a local parameterless `#[test] fn` returning unit.

column3: a standalone Kotodama test module contains a deployable-only item
column4: Keep standalone test modules limited to their target, fixtures, helpers, and #[test] functions.

column3: a standalone Kotodama test file did not declare a module
column4: Declare a module source unit and identify the tested seiyaku with koto_test.

column3: test code reached a production check or build
column4: Move #[test] functions, fixtures, and `test::` calls into a `<name>.test.ko` module that declares `koto_test { target: "..." }`, and run it with `koto test`; production checks and builds reject test code instead of stripping it, so the artifact always matches the reviewed source.

column3: the exact rejection helper requires a typed error variant or rejection selector
column4: Pass an ErrorEnum::Variant value or a test::Rejection selector to expected.

column3: a standalone test module resolves to a different target source
column4: Correct koto_test.target so its normalized path names the graph's exact seiyaku target.

column3: a standalone Kotodama test module omitted its tested seiyaku
column4: Add one koto_test declaration naming the seiyaku under test.

column3: a trigger event cannot supply the callback parameter record
column4: Time, data, and pipeline callbacks take no parameters; read dynamic event data with `context::trigger_event()`. Execute-trigger callbacks may declare typed parameters validated against the explicit event arguments.

column3: a trigger data filter repeats one matcher key
column4: Keep at most one matcher for each supported key in the trigger filter.

column3: a trigger data-filter matcher contains an invalid typed identifier literal
column4: Replace the matcher value with a canonical literal of the identifier type named by the diagnostic.

column3: a trigger data family does not support the requested event kind
column4: Choose one event kind supported by that data family or omit the event restriction.

column3: a trigger data family does not support the requested matcher
column4: Remove the matcher or use a matcher supported by the selected data family.

column3: a trigger authority is not a canonical AccountId
column4: Use a canonical domainless AccountId for trigger authority.

column3: an execute-trigger target is not a canonical TriggerId name
column4: Use a valid canonical Name for the referenced trigger id.

column3: a trigger metadata key is not a canonical Name
column4: Replace the metadata key with a valid canonical Name.

column3: a trigger declaration name is not canonical
column4: Rename the trigger using a valid canonical Name.

column3: a trigger metadata expression cannot be represented as canonical JSON
column4: Use an exactly representable literal or explicit native Json construction.

column3: a schedule argument is positional, mislabelled, or out of order
column4: Write `schedule(start_ms: START, period_ms: PERIOD)` using compile-time integer expressions in milliseconds; the period may be omitted for a one-shot schedule.

column3: a schedule time is not a compile-time integer expression
column4: Use integer constants and checked integer arithmetic for start_ms and period_ms; dynamic function calls are not schedule constants.

column3: a schedule period is zero, negative, or out of range
column4: Use period_ms in 1..=18446744073709551615 milliseconds; omit period_ms for a one-shot schedule.

column3: a schedule start does not fit unsigned 64-bit milliseconds
column4: Use start_ms in 0..=18446744073709551615 milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

column3: a trigger callback does not target a kotoage/言挙げ function
column4: Point the trigger at a declared kotoage/言挙げ function.

column3: a trigger callback names an unauthenticated remote namespace
column4: Use a local kotoage/言挙げ function. A module import does not authenticate a deployed seiyaku interface.

column3: a trigger callback targets a read-only view function
column4: Point the trigger at a declared kotoage/言挙げ function instead.

column3: a tuple member index is outside the tuple's declared fields
column4: Use a zero-based tuple index smaller than the tuple length.

column3: an explicitly typed binding received a value of another type
column4: Keep type-first annotations exact and use only explicit V1 conversions.

column3: collection iteration is not compiler-proven bounded
column4: Iterate a List with capacity at most 64; use map.page(after: cursor, limit: N) or map.take(N) with a compile-time integer expression in 1..=64.

column3: a loop bound is not compiler-proven
column4: Use a static range or a collection operation whose 64-item cap is proven by the compiler.

column3: a qualified call targets a function absent from the package export table
column4: Export the exact function from one module or call a declared exported symbol.

column3: a named type is absent from the explicit package exports
column4: Export the struct or error declaration from its locked package and use the configured import alias.

column3: the source contains U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085
column4: Delete the character or use a normal line break; inside a string literal, write it as a `\\u{...}` escape. These characters end a line in many viewers but not in Kotodama.

column3: a call through a compiler-owned namespace names no builtin
column4: Use a builtin of that namespace; the diagnostic suggests the closest spelling, including the branded spelling of English concept words such as `entrypoint` (kotoage/言挙げ).

column3: the named variant is absent from the nominal enum
column4: Use a variant declared by this exact enum; variant names are case-sensitive.

column3: emit names no declared native event
column4: Declare the event in this seiyaku or an included declaration fragment, then supply its exact record fields.

column3: a qualified call uses an alias not imported by its source package
column4: Add one explicit import binding for the alias or correct the qualified call.

column3: a named argument does not match a declared parameter
column4: Use one of the callee's declared parameter names.

column3: an import names a package absent from the locked graph
column4: Add the exact package identity to the lock graph or correct the import.

column3: authorization or a grant references an undeclared permission
column4: Use a permission declared by this seiyaku or one of its included files. Chain tokens require an explicit `import permission` declaration.

column3: a struct literal refers to an unknown type
column4: Declare the struct in this source unit or import its typed module declaration.

column3: a struct literal names an undeclared field
column4: Use only fields declared by the struct type.

column3: a `while`, `loop` or three-clause `for (init; condition; step)` loop is used
column4: Every loop is a `for` loop whose bound the compiler proves: iterate `range(N)` with a compile-time `N` or a bounded collection, and exit early with `break`.

column3: `&`, `|`, `++` or a closure is used; Kotodama has no such operator
column4: Boolean AND and OR are `&&` and `||`; increment with `+= 1`. Kotodama has no references, bitwise operators or closures; call a named `fn` instead of a closure.

column3: the prior upgrade artifact failed canonical admission
column4: Use the previously deployed complete .to artifact as the upgrade base.

column3: the replacement does not preserve the deployed durable state schema
column4: Preserve every existing state name and complete type; new scalar state requires kaizen and initialized runtime values.

column3: a public view has no explicit caller policy
column4: Choose a declared permission or `authorize(anyone)` before the return type.

column3: a module graph requests a wildcard import
column4: Replace the wildcard with explicit package aliases and exported function names.

column3: a ZK-only operation was retained without ZK compilation policy
column4: Build the seiyaku with explicit ZK project policy or remove the ZK-only operation.

column3: the requested source could not be read
column4: Check that the path exists, is a regular readable file, and contains valid UTF-8.

column3: source exceeds the 1 MiB V1 limit
column4: Split the source into typed modules and compile one deployable seiyaku per file.

column3: source exceeds the 250,000-token V1 limit
column4: Reduce generated source or move reusable declarations into typed modules.

column3: source exceeds the 256-level nesting limit
column4: Flatten nested expressions, types, or blocks.

column3: the diagnostic fanout limit was reached
column4: Fix the reported errors, then rerun the compiler to reveal any remaining failures.

column3: the source contains an invalid token or character
column4: Remove or replace the highlighted text; the message names what the lexer found.

column3: the source does not match the V1 grammar
column4: Compare the highlighted code with the shape the message names; each declaration and statement form is listed in the V1 grammar.

column3: a source package or test graph exceeds a fixed V1 frontend budget
column4: Reduce the number or aggregate byte size of the source files in the graph.

column3: a declaration duplicates or shadows another symbol
column4: Give every declaration and binding a unique, non-reserved name.

column3: a name, type, function, or import could not be resolved
column4: Correct the spelling or add an explicit typed-module import/export.

column3: an expression violates the strict type rules
column4: Use the exact declared type and an explicit conversion operation where one exists.

column3: authorization or view-effect policy was violated
column4: Give every kotoage (言挙げ) an `authorize(Admin)` clause, and keep every function a `view fn` calls free of state writes, ledger instructions, and host effects.

column3: durable-state rules were violated
column4: Initialize scalar state in hajimari and access StateMap values through its typed API.

column3: a recursive call graph or recursive value type was found
column4: Refactor the cycle into an iterative, compiler-proven bounded design.

column3: a function exceeds a V1 argument or result table bound
column4: Reduce the recursively flattened argument or result representation to at most 8192 words per table.

column3: a named value type exceeds a fixed V1 resolution budget
column4: Shorten deeply nested value types or replace repeatedly branching product fields with a flatter bounded schema.

column3: an accepted parameter type retained no bounded ABI representation
column4: Report this compiler defect with the source; semantic analysis must assign every parameter an exact bounded V1 ABI representation.

column3: resolved-HIR construction or integrity validation failed
column4: Report this compiler defect with the source; resolution stopped before typed/effect analysis.

column3: the program violates the deterministic on-chain profile
column4: Remove test-only or non-deterministic behavior from the deployable seiyaku.

column3: a typed construct has no V1 code-generation form
column4: Use a supported V1 type or operation; this is a compiler defect if the grammar promises the construct.

column3: typed HIR could not be lowered to SSA MIR
column4: Simplify the reported construct and report a compiler defect if valid V1 source triggered it.

column3: SSA optimization failed to preserve a valid deterministic control-flow graph
column4: Report this compiler defect with a minimal source reproducer; no artifact is emitted after an optimizer failure.

column3: lowered IR could not be converted into validated SSA form
column4: Report this compiler defect with a minimal source reproducer; valid typed HIR must always produce validated SSA.

column3: optimized SSA could not be converted back into validated lowering IR
column4: Report this compiler defect with a minimal source reproducer; no bytecode is emitted from an invalid optimized program.

column3: bytecode generation failed
column4: When the message names a source construct (for example an argument that must be a literal), fix that construct. Any other message describes a compiler defect, not a problem in the source: report it with a minimal source reproducer. Valid V1 programs always assemble deterministically.

column3: compiler-owned artifact preparation failed
column4: Report a compiler defect; source cannot override ABI or execution-header policy.

column3: manifest or deployable artifact construction failed
column4: Report a compiler defect and do not deploy a partial output.

column3: a reusable module was requested as a deployable artifact
column4: Link the module into exactly one seiyaku root and build that seiyaku.

column3: durable state is declared but never used
column4: Remove the declaration or read/write it from a reachable function.

column3: a declaration shadows durable state
column4: Rename the declaration; strict V1 source should keep every binding unambiguous.

column3: a private function parameter is never used
column4: Remove the parameter or use it in the function body; prefix its name with `_` to keep it deliberately. Parameters of kotoage, view, and lifecycle declarations are argument keys of the public interface and are not reported.
column5: fn fee(int amount, int unused) -> int {\n    return amount;\n}
column6: fn fee(int amount) -> int {\n    return amount;\n}

column3: a statement is unreachable after return
column4: Delete the unreachable statement or move it before the terminating return.

column3: the same typed literal is repeated in one seiyaku
column4: Declare the value once as a named `const` and refer to it by name, so every use is identical and reviewers can see what the literal stands for.

column3: a constructed typed value is never used
column4: Remove the constructor call or use its result.

column3: a trigger specification is not statically transparent
column4: Use a canonical literal trigger specification so admission can derive its behavior.

column3: a state path is dynamic without complete access metadata
column4: Use a canonical StateMap operation or a literal state path when scheduler precision matters.

column3: an opaque operation prevents precise access derivation
column4: Prefer typed namespaced operations with derivable access; otherwise execution is serialized conservatively.

column3: a copy of durable state is changed but never written back
column4: Reading a StateMap entry or a whole state value returns a copy. Store the changed copy with `Map[key] = value;` (or `state = value;`) after the last change, or the change is lost when the call ends.

column3: a kotoage performs no state, ledger, or host effects
column4: Declare it `view fn` so callers can query it without a transaction or fee. A view may keep `authorize(Admin)` to restrict who may call it.
column5: permission Entry; kotoage fn add(int a, int b) authorize(Entry) -> int {\n    return a + b;\n}
column6: view fn add(int a, int b) authorize(anyone) -> int {\n    return a + b;\n}

column3: exact decimal or quantity division by a runtime value can revert
column4: Exact `/` rejects quotients that do not terminate within 28 fractional digits, such as 1/3. Divide with an explicit rounding mode through `div_round`, `ratio_round`, or `mul_div_round`, choosing the scale and mode the seiyaku requires.
column6: return total.div_round(divisor: parts, scale: 6, mode: Rounding::floor);

column3: a local binding is never read
column4: Remove the binding or use it; bind to `_` to evaluate an expression only for its effects.

column3: a stored value is overwritten before it is read
column4: Remove the earlier store, or read the value before assigning the binding again.

column3: a public parameter name starts with an underscore
column4: Public parameter names are the argument keys callers send, so a leading `_` becomes part of the interface. Rename the parameter; public parameters are never reported as unused, so the prefix silences nothing.

column3: a `var` binding is never reassigned or mutated
column4: Declare the binding with `let`; `var` marks a binding that a later assignment, compound assignment, field write, or mutating method changes.

column3: a private function is never called
column4: Remove the function, call it, or prefix its name with `_` to keep it deliberately. In a module, declare it `export fn` when other units need it.

column3: a seiyaku declares no kotoage, view, or lifecycle function
column4: Private `fn` helpers run only when a public function calls them, so nothing can call this seiyaku. Add a kotoage/言挙げ function with `authorize(Admin)` for state changes, or a `view fn` for queries.
column5: seiyaku Quiet {\n    fn helper() -> int { return 1; }\n}
column6: seiyaku Quiet {\n    view fn value() authorize(anyone) -> int { return 1; }\n}

column3: a linter finding lacked a dedicated unified diagnostic code
column4: Report the finding so it can receive a stable K5000-series code and remediation.

column3: reachable private inputs require local prover witness transport unavailable in production
column4: Separate local proof generation from the deployable contract; production hosts cannot supply private test witnesses.
